title: The Ultimate Reverse-Seared Cowboy Ribeye

source.name: How To Reverse Sear A Steak: Step-by-Step Recipe - Allen Brothers

ingredients.name: coarse kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper

steps: Pat the ribeye completely dry with paper towels. Season generously on all sides with kosher salt and black pepper; let rest on a wire rack uncovered in the refrigerator for 2 to 4 hours to dry the surface.
Preheat the oven to 250°F (121°C) and place the steak on the wire rack set inside a rimmed baking sheet.
Roast in the oven for 25 to 30 minutes until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center reads 115°F (for medium-rare finish).
Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot. Add the neutral oil.
Sear the steak for 45 to 90 seconds on the first side until a deep mahogany crust forms. Flip and sear the second side for 45 seconds.
Sear the exterior fat cap edge for 30 seconds to render the fat.
Reduce heat to medium-low, add butter, smashed garlic, and fresh herb sprigs. Tilt the pan and spoon foaming herb butter continuously over the steak for 1 minute.
Transfer to a warm cutting board, rest for 5 to 7 minutes, slice against the grain, and serve.
swaps: Can substitute thick-cut New York strip or Porterhouse steak; canola oil works if avocado oil is unavailable.
notes: The gold standard for thick-cut steak: edge-to-edge pink doneness with a restaurant-grade crust.

title: Grilled T-Bone Steak with Herb Seasoning

ingredients.name: kosher salt and cracked black pepper

steps: Trim excess exterior fat on steak to 1/4 inch to prevent flare-ups on the grill.
Rub steak with olive oil, minced garlic, dried oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper; let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Preheat gas or charcoal grill to medium-high heat (approx. 400°F).
Place steak on hot grill grates. Grill for 5 to 6 minutes on the first side.
Flip steak once using tongs (do not pierce with a fork). Grill for another 5 to 6 minutes until internal temperature reaches 135°F for medium-rare (or 145°F for medium).
Transfer steak to a platter, tent loosely with aluminum foil, and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
swaps: Can use ribeye or strip steak; fresh herbs can replace dried herbs.
notes: Classic outdoor grilling technique. Trimming fat and flipping only once ensures even charring without soot.

title: Cast-Iron Seared Flat Iron Steak with Garlic Butter

source.name: BEEF COOKERY - NDBeef
source.location: Section: Skillet Cookery & Flat Iron Steaks, Page 8

ingredients.name: coarse sea salt and cracked black pepper

steps: Pat flat iron steak dry with paper towels; season both sides generously with sea salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place steak in hot skillet and sear for 3 to 4 minutes without moving until a golden-brown crust forms.
Flip steak, add butter and minced garlic to the skillet, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes on the second side.
Spoon melted garlic butter over the steak continuously while finishing cooking (target 135°F for medium-rare).
Remove steak from pan to a warm board, rest for 5 minutes, and carve into thin diagonal slices across the grain.
swaps: Top sirloin or flank steak can substitute for flat iron steak.
notes: Flat iron is one of the most tender, flavorful cuts when cooked hot and fast in cast iron.

title: Grilled Ribeye with Ancho Chili Bourbon Butter
steps: In a small bowl, beat softened butter with bourbon, 1/2 teaspoon ancho chili powder, a pinch of salt, and pepper until emulsified; roll in plastic wrap and chill into a compound butter log.
Brush ribeye steaks with olive oil and rub with remaining ancho chili powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Preheat grill or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Grill steaks for 4 to 5 minutes on the first side until charred grill marks appear.
Flip steaks and grill for 4 minutes on the second side until internal temperature reaches 130°F to 135°F for medium-rare.
Transfer steaks to plates, top each immediately with a thick round of cold ancho-bourbon butter, and rest for 5 minutes as the butter melts into a rich glaze.
swaps: Beef broth can replace bourbon in the compound butter for an alcohol-free option.
notes: The bold smokiness of ancho chili and rich bourbon butter enhances the marbling of prime ribeye.

title: Pan-Seared T-Bone with Peach-Tarragon Reduction

ingredients.name: dry white wine or dry vermouth

steps: Season T-bone steak generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Sear steak for 4 to 5 minutes per side until browned and cooked to medium-rare (135°F).
Transfer steak to a plate and tent loosely with foil to rest.
Drain excess fat from skillet, leaving 1 tablespoon of drippings. Add diced peach and cook for 2 minutes until lightly caramelized.
Pour in white wine and beef stock, scraping up fond from the pan bottom. Simmer vigorously for 3 minutes until reduced to a syrupy glaze.
Stir in fresh tarragon and pour savory-sweet peach reduction over the rested steak.
swaps: Fresh plums or apricots can substitute for peaches; fresh thyme can replace tarragon.
notes: Gourmet competition dish balancing rich beef fat with fruit acidity and anise-scented tarragon.

title: Filet Mignon Three Ways (Oven-Finished Tenderloin)

ingredients.name: kosher salt and cracked black pepper

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F (205°C). Season filet mignon steaks generously on all sides with kosher salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe cast-iron skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add filets and sear for 2 minutes on the first side without moving. Flip and sear for 2 minutes on second side.
Add butter, crushed garlic, and thyme to pan, spooning melted butter over filets for 30 seconds.
Transfer skillet directly into the 400°F oven and roast for 4 to 5 minutes until internal temperature reaches 125°F–130°F for medium-rare.
Remove from oven, transfer steaks to a warm board, and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
swaps: Can serve with Béarnaise sauce, red wine reduction, or truffle butter.
notes: Classic steakhouse technique ensuring tenderloin develops a deep crust while keeping center velvety.

title: Quick-Broiled Top Sirloin Steak

source.name: Ultimate Guide to Beef | Burgers' Smokehouse
source.location: How to Cook Beef - Broiling Section

steps: Turn oven to high broil setting and preheat for 10 minutes with broiler pan inside.
Pat sirloin steak dry; brush with olive oil and season evenly with garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Carefully place steak on the hot slotted broiler rack (positioned 3 to 4 inches from upper heat element).
Broil for 3 minutes on the first side. Remove pan using an oven mitt, flip steak with tongs, and return to broil for 3 minutes.
Check with an instant-read thermometer to ensure meat reaches 145°F (medium doneness).
Transfer steak to a cutting board, tent with foil, and let rest for 3 to 5 minutes before carving into slices.
swaps: Can use flat iron or ribeye steak in place of top sirloin.
notes: Fastest indoor dry-heat steak method; intense radiant heat replicates restaurant salamanders.

title: Marinated Skirt Steak (Carne Asada Style)

source.name: How to Cook Beef: Best Cooking Method for Every Cut - Clover Meadows Beef
source.location: Flank & Skirt Steak Stir-Frying & Grilling Section

ingredients.name: beef skirt steak or flank steak

steps: In a gallon zip-top bag, combine lime juice, olive oil, minced garlic, cumin, chili powder, cilantro, salt, and pepper. Add skirt steak and marinate in refrigerator for 1 to 4 hours.
Preheat grill or heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot.
Remove skirt steak from marinade, discarding excess liquid; pat exterior lightly with paper towels.
Sear steak over intense high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until charred on exterior and medium-rare (130°F) in center.
Transfer to a cutting board and rest for 5 minutes.
Carve thinly across the grain at a 45-degree bias angle. Serve with warm corn tortillas and fresh lime.
swaps: Flank steak can be used; serve over cilantro-lime rice for a bowl format.
notes: Thin skirt steak must be cooked hot and fast and sliced thinly across the grain to be tender.
